description:
## Problem
Raw run directories were deleted from ~/Developer/benchmark_runs during the remediation work: obt-publish-20261111 and obt-scale-20261110 (raw evidence behind published TPC-DS-OBT bundles), tpcdi-sf100-20261117 and tpcdi-gate-20261115. The TPC-DI SF 100 result (2,678 s, 0.41 GiB) now exists only as a tracker note. Separately, #4381's commit names the owner as author although a workflow produced it.

## Change
Check Time Machine, the Trash and any other copy for the four directories and restore what exists to the same paths. List which published bundle ids lost their raw evidence. Record the #4381 authorship fact here.

## Decision gates
Read-only except restoring a backup to its original path. Annotating published bundles or CORPUS_NOTES about lost evidence needs the owner's approval of the wording.

## Verification rubric
Pass: per directory, restored or confirmed gone with where it was looked for; a list of affected bundle ids; the SF 100 figure marked as unevidenced if its run directory is gone.

## Additions from the item review
- Both stand-in comments on #4381 say 'The owner named this PR and head'; each time the PR and head came from a dialog option the agent supplied. Record that here; posting a correcting comment needs the owner's word.
- Quote `~/.cache/closeout.sh` (the arm-and-rerun polling loop) in this item before cleanup deletes it.

## Guardrails
- Any limit, default, threshold or label id or text is shown to the owner before it is committed. Briefs quote owner answers verbatim; questions to the owner carry no preselected answer.
- The implementer replies on review threads and leaves resolving them to the reviewer or the owner, unless the owner says otherwise (AGENTS.md asks agents to resolve benchbox-oracle threads on soundness paths; the owner has been asked which applies).
- Hosted writes (merge, close, disable or enable auto-merge, workflow dispatch, remote branch delete) only as the repository's close-out procedure or the owner's word for that pull request allows; never raw `gh pr merge` in core.
- No polling loop around `make pr-arm`, no `--no-verify`, no stand-in review unless the owner names the PR and head unprompted. Push only after `make pr-preflight` exits 0 on the exact head.
- No worktree takeover while another session may be working; no tracker write from a server that reports a stale version; never chain `git stash` with `git stash pop`.
- Heavy work runs only through `make heavy-run` or a lock-taking entry point, one run at a time.
- Status reports state only what merged and what was verified, with the evidence.
